quest.title: All Is Foretold
quest.description: Back at base, everyone is discussing what to do next. Then, an unexpected figure enters the conversation.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x1325, Mora x58200, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x11

chapter.num: Song of the Welkin Moon: Act IV
chapter.title: An Elegy for Faded Moonlight

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do you think the others are making good progress? Hope it's all going smoothly...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, look! They made it back as well!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Flins, Lauma! How'd it all go?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: All is well, thank you. Nefer and Jahoda had to stay at the Curatorium to wrap things up, so they won't be joining us for now.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: I ran into Miss Ineffa and Miss Aino on the way back. Their work is still in progress, so I suspect they won't be back for a while either.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: You seem rather cheerful today, Mr. Flins?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: I certainly am. I achieved what I set out to do, and came away with more than I bargained for.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: More than you bargained for?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Fighting alone can get quite tedious, but I had the good fortune to run into a pair of brave young warriors...

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: We meet again. How have you been?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Albedo! What are you doing here?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Thankfully, tracking you down turned out to be a lot simpler than we envisaged.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: These two courageously lent me a hand while I was fighting the Wild Hunt. When they told me they were Sir Varka's colleagues, it all made sense.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: And given how people of outstanding talent tend to cross paths, it's no wonder you're already acquainted.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So... Who's your travel buddy, Albedo?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Why don't you come and introduce yourself?

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Hm. A gentleman of few words, I see. And a rather stern countenance... I presumed you were acquainted with him, is that not the case?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Wait, those horns...You must be...!
It's nice to meet you.... again. We've... technically met before.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait a sec, you're... You're Mini Durin!?

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: That's right. It's me. I'm glad to see you again.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: By the way, he says it's okay if you drop the "Mini."

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Yeah, I'm not as "mini" as I used to be.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Interesting, isn't it? The first step towards blending into human society appears to be reflecting on whether one's name really reflects who they are.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, you look... so different... in a good way, of course! It's great to see you looking so healthy.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Thank you, Paimon... And although you're as mini as ever, I understand that diminutives don't always convey endearment. I'll be sure to simply call you "Paimon" as a sign of my great respect for you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, you're such a smooth talker now... Hehe, Paimon could get used to this. From now on, you may refer to her as your "Esteemed Guide, Paimon"!

choices.text: I actually think a diminutive is warranted here.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Personally, I think our little Paimon is the perfect size.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: When people call her Little Paimon, it's just because she's so adorable that they can't help themselves. If that's not a sign of endearment, what is?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: You're absolutely right, Miss Lauma. My brother still has a long road ahead of him when it comes to understanding human relationships.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Hmm... Anyway, speaking of long journeys, didn't Kuutar — sorry, Columbina, leave with you? How come she isn't back yet?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ahh, she's been catching up with old friends. Hehe, wouldn't be surprised if she stopped for a cup of tea or ten on the way back...

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Uh-oh, people are talking about me? Hope it's nothing negative...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Seems like she's in much better spirits after meeting her old colleagues.)

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Judging from your expressions, I'm guessing it all went well?

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: It's getting crowded here... I'll go grab some chairs.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: No need... this is a job for an alchemist. I'll whip some up momentarily.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Thank you for your hospitality, ladies and gentlemen, but I was merely escorting my friends back.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: I'll be meeting Sandrone shortly, as we still have some things to discuss. It's been a pleasure, everyone, but this is where I'll say goodbye.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: We really appreciate your help.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Thanks for standing by us.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Come on, spare the formalities. I'm just glad I could help out some true friends.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: I understand. Well... Bye for now, Arlecchino.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Hohoho, this place is hopping! It's probably a good thing one of us left, otherwise we might not fit all these people in...

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Are you saying we're about to run out of chairs?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: As a matter of fact, I am... Come on in and see for yourself.

choices.text: Little Paimon is pretty tiny, after all.
I'm guessing you're here to see Varka?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: That would be a natural assumption to make. It's also the correct one.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: I overheard your little chit-chat outside, by the way. With Miss Columbina's colleague gone, we should be back to the original crew plus the other colleagues I brought in.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Though it looks like we have another new face... Someone else manage to rope in a colleague, too?

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: Frankly, you and Paimon are the only people I know here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #This here is Dainsleif, colleague of Teyvat's greatest guide, Paimon and greatest adventurer, {NICKNAME}! ...Well, not exactly colleagues. More sort of... friends.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: When someone else jumps in to do the announcing, you know you're speaking to someone important.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Let's hear what he has to say.

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: (Tch... Note to self, once Paimon knows your name, the rest of the world will soon follow.)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: When he comes looking for us, it's usually something important. Paimon's guessing you've heard about the Wild Hunt, then?

response.speaker: Dainsleif
response.text: From the looks of it, you're about to hold a meeting. If I were to say that the Wild Hunt is our mutual enemy... would that earn me a seat at the table?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: As the saying goes, the enemy of my enemy is my friend. Mr. Dainsleif, there's a seat with your name on it.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Though, I can't promise the same for everyone else... Albedo, think you can rustle up a couple more chairs?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: After all this time apart, Grand Master Varka's first order is to "rustle up a couple more chairs." Ah, I've missed this.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: ...Is he being sarcastic?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, he's your brother! Why are you asking us?

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: I've still got a lot to learn about the nuances of human conversation. Trying to decipher Albedo's way of speaking has been like jumping in at the deep end...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ohhh, good point, Paimon gets you now. Don't sweat it, there are people who go their whole lives without getting the hang of it. You're ahead of the game already!

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: I wonder what's taking Nefer so long...

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Perhaps you should go and check in with her? If anyone can hurry her along, it's you.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: I just got back from the Curatorium. Besides, aren't you curious to see what's taking her so long?

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Miss Nefer doesn't strike me as the type to share secrets — and since gathering intel is her specialty, I'm guessing she'd prefer to keep her methods confidential.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Under such circumstances, would it not be tactless for me to impose?

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Oh, but it's fine for me to impose?

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: What can I say? You have an unrivaled ability to garner people's affection, Miss Moonchanter. Besides, you have far more in common with her than I do.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: *sigh*... Alright then.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Impressive. She barely fought back at all... I admire your powers of persuasion, my friend.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: As I'm sure Miss Lauma will realize soon enough, the trick in life is to always pitch in with other people's responsibilities so that you can be selective with your own.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Another trick is to simply hide in the background.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Spoken like a true sage.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Anyway, looks like we've got some time to kill before the meeting. Let's take a little breather, folks.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Feel free to chat amongst yourselves. We'll get down to business once the other two arrive.

talks.objective: Chat with everyone while you're waiting

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: You're both awfully quiet. Why don't I start us off with an icebreaker?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Much obliged.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Have either of you ever had your portrait painted? If not, I'd be glad to help.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: That sounds like a lovely idea. You know how to paint, then?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I dabble occasionally.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: He's an excellent painter. Tables, chairs, people, dragons... You name it, he'll paint it for you.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I'm flattered.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: If I ever get the chance, I'd like to give it a try myself.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I'll bear that in mind. Anyway, how about you, Durin? What sort of portrait would you prefer?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Oh, I'd be fine with anything.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Whatever style feels best to you.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Very well. Then, I'll play it by ear.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: You can replicate any style I want?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I can try. If you show me a sample, I'll do my best to match it.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Thank you... In that case, I'll dig up some reference material for you.

talks.objective: Chat with everyone while you're waiting

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Is there... something you'd like to say to me?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! For starters, why did you just show up here without even giving us a heads-up!?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: If you think back to our previous interactions, you may recall that that's hardly out-of-character for me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You... do have a point there.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sorted out your accommodation yet?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ohhh, yeah — you'll need to find somewhere to stay the night too, right? Wanna tag along with us? You never know, we might get a group discount...

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Sure. Let's do that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Great! Paimon will handle it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, and in return, we can get Dainsleif to be our very own personal bodyguard!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Paimon, you're thinking out loud again...

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: If that's what you had in mind, you should have said so sooner. I'd be happy to help.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, okay then... Heh, Paimon was only kidding but... Good to know!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Anyway, since we're all here together, we might as well watch each other's backs. That's just what friends do, right?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: ...Indeed. Thank you.

talks.objective: Chat with everyone while you're waiting

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Truth be told, I can't remember the last time I was in a meeting with so many people.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: You're not alone there, my friend. The Lightkeepers also struggle to bring everyone together for a serious discussion.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Hahaha, I don't doubt that. I've only ever met two Ratniki — one being you, and the other being that young guy, Illuga.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Illuga's a good apple, I'll give him that. He's kind, honest, and regularly delivers supplies to my lighthouse. A true Ratnik to the core... In that sense, he puts me to shame.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Haha, so you're what — a fake Ratnik? That's what it sounds like you're saying... But I get the feeling that's not quite what you meant.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: C'mon, why the awkward silence?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Sorry, I'm not even gonna bother trying to hide it. You've known all along, haven't you, my friend?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Aha... Now that was an awkward silence.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Let's just keep this between ourselves. Probably best if Illuga doesn't know, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: That goes without saying. Gotta be careful what you share with youngsters, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: #Anyone else in the know? Let me guess... {NICKNAME} and Paimon?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: It's dangerous being too sharp for one's own good, you know.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Then in the name of the Anemo Archon, Barbatos himself, I swear your secret's safe with me.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Hmm... When we went for drinks, you said that you and Barbatos were "practically best buds." In the light of that claim, do you really expect me to take your oath seriously?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Of course! Just as long as you don't go spreading around the fact that I'm close with Barbatos, alright?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Hm, fair enough then. Nothing like a bit of mutual leverage to seal the bonds of friendship.
But surely you can see he's not the man he pretends to be! So many have died already, and they say that the king's madness grows with each passing day...
We're not going to survive this, are we? But... why does it have to be this way? Do we really deserve to die just because of the blood that runs through our veins?
Tholindis, are you even listening!?

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: Ah... Sorry, Frithr. My mind was off wandering.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: I heard you, though... You're talking about what Rerir said.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: He's just following the king's orders. He's a secret agent, and it's his job to hunt down rebels and dissidents.

dialogues.speaker: Frithr
dialogues.text: By the time you first met him, he'd already taken lives! Maybe he was using you from the very beginning?

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: No. Rerir has no idea I have anything to do with the Crimson Moon. My family are only distant relatives of the main lineage, and besides, my eyes are perfectly ordinary.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: Truth be told, apart from my teacher, pretty much no one knows I have any connection to any of it. It's been a long time since my family severed ties.

dialogues.speaker: Frithr
dialogues.text: But as Orlog said, who could possibly talk sense into that raving lunatic of a king? No one...

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: I'll work something out... Trust me, I'm with you all. But for now, you need to keep yourselves hidden. Don't let anyone find you, anyone at all.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: Don't forget that Rerir is an Eclipse operative. You need to be extra careful when he's around... and when I am too.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: For now, don't come looking for me. And if anything happens to me, just act like we've never met.

dialogues.speaker: Frithr
dialogues.text: If even you can't escape this, what hope do the rest of us have? But after all this time together... surely he wouldn't lay a hand on you?

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: I won't speak in his defense, nor can I give you a clear answer to that question. But I'll do everything I can to put an end to this.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: Here, hold onto this. If an opportunity to escape presents itself, take it. You'll be glad you took some spare change.

dialogues.speaker: Frithr
dialogues.text: Uh... You call that "change"!? I... Uh... But what about you?

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: I've got a job, and there's still money coming in, but you can't go anywhere right now. Please, think about yourself for once.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Ah, Miss Nefer! You made it after all.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: But what about Jahoda?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I'm here to give you an update on how things are going on our end. Once this is over, I'll be heading straight back to continue my work. I left Jahoda back at the Curatorium to watch over things while I'm gone.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Heh, so much for "just this once"...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Shh, not so loud! We're on a roll here... What if she remembers and suddenly decides to back out!?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: ...Did you say something, Mr. Varka?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Huh? I didn't say anything... right, Flins?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Hmm, must have been a frog. They get so noisy around here at nighttime, it's like they're putting on a concert in the background.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Anyway... Before we begin, there's a few introductions to make. Let me start by saying that it's an honor to be speaking before so many distinguished colleagues and collaborators.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: First up, we have Miss Lauma. As Moonchanter, she's the leader of the Frostmoon Scions, a local religious community in Nod-Krai. Then there's Miss Nefer, boss of the Curatorium of Secrets, and intel-gatherer extraordinaire.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Nefer is leading the investigation into Rerir's background, assisted by Jahoda and Lauma. From the little I've heard, they're making some great progress.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Over here, we have Mr. Flins — a Ratnik, and guardian of the abandoned lighthouse. In our last operation, he courageously distracted the Wild Hunt to buy time for the rest of us.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: For those of you who've never met, this is Mr. Albedo, a renowned alchemist and Captain of the Knights of Favonius Investigation Team. By his side is a new face for us all, myself included — Mr. Durin, who has come to lend his aid.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Next up, we have the Moon Maiden and former Fatui Harbinger, Miss Columbina.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: #Then we have {NICKNAME} — who's earned more titles than I can possibly hope to list out, so I'll spare you the rundown — and Paimon, the ultimate travel companion and quite possibly the best guide in all of Teyvat.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, that's a lot of people. Great turnout!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Miss Nefer, it looks like you might have another job coming your way. So uh... congratulations on the booming business, I guess...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: ...You think I haven't got enough on my hands as it is? Who's looking for me now?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: That would be me, Miss Nefer. I have a commission for you.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: And you are?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Who I am doesn't matter right now. What does matter is that I'd like you to gather more intelligence about the Rächer of Solnari.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Hmm, well it's not as if we never take on anonymous commissions... but in your case, I'll have to decline. I'm gonna take a wild guess and say your job's probably more hassle than it's worth. Something about you seems like bad news.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: It's my eyes, isn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Khaenri'ahn, I assume? And what's with the mask — are you trying to hide your identity? In any case, the fact that you're even still alive raises an awful lot of questions for me.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: My name is Dainsleif — and yes, I am from Khaenri'ah. As I'm sure you're aware the Rächer of Solnari's real name is Rerir. He was once... an acquaintance of mine.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Really? Then you must have been quite an influential figure yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: You flatter me, but none of that matters anymore. My point was simply to clarify why I have asked Miss Nefer to investigate Rerir's background.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: So you're both from Khaenri'ah, and it sounds like you used to be friends? What am I missing here? Surely, you already know how he became one of the Five Sinners?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: I'll tell you everything I know. The history of Khaenri'ah, the names and identities of the Five Sinners... I remember it all like it was yesterday.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: I have never spoken openly of this before, but the truth was exactly as people say. The Five Sinners were each driven by their own desires, and it was by playing upon these that the Abyss tempted them to their fall, tearing Khaenri'ah apart in the process.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: The Visionary Vedrfolnir, who wished to foretell the future. "The Wise" Hroptatyr, who sought limitless knowledge.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Gold Rhinedottir, who desired to create life. "The Foul" Surtalogi, who pursued supreme strength.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: And last, but not least, "Rächer of Solnari" Rerir... ravager of the moon.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Of the five, Rerir is the only one who remains a mystery to me. He never harbored grand ambitions — so what changed in the space of a single night? How did he come to fall like the others?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: In other words, you're saying that his change came as a shock to you, and you have no idea what actually happened?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: That's right.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: You mentioned how the Abyss tempted them, which led to their fall... But what did that look like in practice? And what other context can you give me about the events of that time? The more detail you can give me, the better.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: ...Strangely, now that it comes to it, I hardly know where to begin.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: The fateful night took place during the era of the Eclipse Dynasty. One day, my elder brother, "The Visionary" Vedrfolnir, was summoned to the palace by the Vinster King — only for the king to gouge out his eyes and cast him into the dungeons.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: When I came to hear of this, my fury knew no bounds. I gathered together every ally I thought I had, and together, we set a night to storm the palace and free Ved.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: ...Centuries on, the memories of that night still haunt me like a never-ending nightmare. We broke through the palace gates, just like we had planned, each striking towards our separate targets...

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: ...But then, I was betrayed. Even Vedrfolnir — the very person I had come to rescue — abandoned me and partook of the Abyss's power.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: So it's personal, after all. Then tell me, Mr. Dainsleif — what price are you willing to pay? You of all people must know that nothing comes for free.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: I cannot say what price would be worthy of such a commission... But know this: Rerir was not always a madman. Believe it or not, there was a time when he was just an ordinary man, working for the Khaenri'ahn intelligence service.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Uncovering the truth of Rerir's past is the only way to unravel this mystery. But before you decide if you will accept my commission, I will tell you more about him — enough, I hope, to help you plan your next move.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Sounds pretty good to me. Hahaha, feels like we just flagged down a random passerby, only to discover he's actually a master strategist who has a score to settle with our enemy...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Not long after...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: So that's how the Rächer of Solnari was born.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Hmph... A monster created by circumstance is a monster all the same.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (Viewing other people's thoughts for too long can get uncomfortable. Right now, I'm feeling a strong sense of loathing.)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (In a nutshell, the story of Khaenri'ah is what happens when the truth falls by the wayside. Everyone tells little white lies, and before long, you have a huge pack of lies that destroys everything.)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Phew... Time to get back.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (His past is filled with sorrow, but the tale of any fallen civilization is one of endless tragedy. Cruel as it may be, that was Khaenri'ah's fate.)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Thank you for waiting.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's okay! We actually used the time to help Dainsleif get a room at the hotel.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: That's very considerate of you.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Now — I trust you share my curiosity about Rerir's past? And you seem fairly familiar with Mr. Dainsleif already.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's right. We've known each other for quite some time now.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: We spoke at some length after the meeting. He was the one who suggested I should invite you to join this operation. He feels confident that these secrets will be safe with you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Dain has a lot of faith in us, that's for sure.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thanks for your trust too, Nefer.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Likewise. I appreciate that you got right on board without interrogating me about why I invited you. It shows that you trust me to explain everything in due course.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, that's 'cause we know what you're capable of! We appreciate you too, Nefer. You might've been forced to help in the beginning, but this time, it was your choice!

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: That's one way to put it. Another is this — that once a decision's been made, it's set in stone. After that, my only goal is to see it through.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Alright... So here's how it is. I'm going to access Rerir's thoughts again using my confidential method. Now, I'm sure you've seen things like this before on your travels, so you're surely well aware of how dangerous it can be.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: The reason I've gathered you all here is to ensure my safety during the proceedings. I plan for us to enter the fragment of his consciousness together, and once inside, I will focus on searching for information.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Think of this as a diving expedition into someone's brain. If I'm the diver, you are my safety equipment, tasked with keeping me alive while I'm under the surface.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Once the ceremony begins, we will all be spying on privileged information. But in the interests of safety, you must remain absolutely silent at all times. We will discuss our observations after the ceremony has concluded.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Lastly, any individuals of a weaker constitution are advised not to partake in the ceremony. In any case, Paimon has her own job to do, which requires staying in the room but not joining the ceremony.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Nefer conspicuously left out the details of her "confidential method"...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I guess her brain-diving techniques are a trade secret.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, good luck everyone. Sounds like all Paimon can do is cross her fingers and root for you guys...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: There's a little more to it than that. I was being serious when I said you have a job to do. While the rest of us are inside Rerir's mind, it's imperative that we have a team member on the outside.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: In the event that something goes wrong, you will be our first responder. I don't anticipate any issues, but the extra level of safety will be greatly appreciated.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: I second that. This is a dangerous operation here, and you're our whole rescue team. That's pretty much the most important job in the crew!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, Paimon's like... the lifeguard? ...Yeah, that makes sense. Alright, got it!

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Good. Please take a seat, we'll get started momentarily.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: So, did Mr. Dainsleif tell you anything else?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: He told me that he believes Rerir kept some big secrets in his life. He's not sure that they were the cause of his eventual downfall, but he's asked me to uncover what those secrets were all the same.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: But surely you're not planning to go through with this no matter the cost?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: If you think that, you'd be overestimating me. I'm a businesswoman, not a mercenary.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: But I do have my own professional reasons for taking this job. You think I'd turn down the opportunity to get a first-hand glimpse into Khaenri'ahn history? No chance.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Well, as long as you don't let morbid curiosity get in the way of safety concerns, we're good. We'll do whatever we can to help you.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Tch, you're such a killjoy.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (She's got incense, candles... Almost feels like a summoning ritual.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Seems like Nefer still has no intention of sharing her trade secrets. But now's not exactly the moment to pry...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I see there's a chess set on the table... Could that have something to do with her intel-gathering methods?)

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Alright, I'm good to go.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: All set over here too.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm ready as well.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Promise Paimon you'll be extra careful!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Pinky promise.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Alright, let your whole body relax. We're about to begin.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Close your eyes.

dialogues.speaker: Frithr
dialogues.text: Y—You're really letting me go?

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: I am. As long as you can guarantee that no one will find you.

dialogues.speaker: Frithr
dialogues.text: Don't worry, I'll be extra careful... No one will know I was here.

dialogues.speaker: Frithr
dialogues.text: B—But... What about you?

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Me?

dialogues.speaker: Frithr
dialogues.text: If you let me go, you won't be able to complete your mission, will you?

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Hmm, good point. In that case, maybe you should stay.

dialogues.speaker: Frithr
dialogues.text: No, please! I just... want to see the outside world again. To...

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: ...Go on living?

dialogues.speaker: Frithr
dialogues.text: Yes! I know you're a man of your word... So please, just let me go.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: If I let you leave, what will become of me?

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: ...Just kidding. Go now.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: But remember, don't let anyone know you were caught. We'll be seeing each other again very soon if you do.

dialogues.speaker: Abyssal Whisper
dialogues.text: Even shadows in the dark must live by a code. But you can't save everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: You've been whispering in my ear for days now, Vedrfolnir. What are you trying to do? Break me down?

dialogues.speaker: Abyssal Whisper
dialogues.text: I only say this because you long for an answer to your problems: Let her go, Rerir, or you risk losing everything.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: I will not abandon Tholindis.

dialogues.speaker: Abyssal Whisper
dialogues.text: Then you'll need a little more vigilance, and a lot more power. The world is changing, Rerir... Keep your eyes peeled for your moment of opportunity.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: (That voice used to be so unclear, but now I know exactly whose it is. It's Vedrfolnir.)

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: (He won't tell me how to actually resolve any of this, but he keeps trying to manipulate me like a puppet. What's his game here?)

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Tell me, then, what will this "moment of opportunity" look like?

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: (And... no answer. He's like a ghost — always disturbing me when I'm on edge, but never answering when I need him most.)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: So, the Eclipse Dynasty was purging... well, massacring the descendants of the Crimson Moon. And it seems like it was all connected to the Vinster King's research.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: The king's obsession with Abyssal power left the future of Khaenri'ah hanging in the balance. No wonder every aspect of Rerir's life was so unstable...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: And it looks like this Tholindis, Rerir's would-be fiancee, herself belonged to a sub-branch of the Crimson Moon dynasty's descendants...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: It almost defies belief that a couple like them could hide the truth from each other for so long. If the Vinster King hadn't intervened in such a drastic way, they might have gone on deceiving each other for the rest of their lives.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: And why does Vedrfolnir, Dainsleif's older brother, keep talking in Rerir's head? Huh... This guy kept more secrets than I ever imagined.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: The human mind is like a vast desert of shifting sands. When you follow the flow of someone's memories, you only ever see the parts they're willing to let surface.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Time for something a bit more creative.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: We've been inside Rerir's mind this whole time, building up a picture of his psyche.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: There's already enough clues on the board to start reading between the lines and mapping out the rest.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Now, we can finally begin to put the pieces together. Sure, it'll only be a reconstruction — part simulation, part reasoning. But it's usually pretty accurate.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Once we've built up a cognitive profile, we just need to cross-check the logic behind his actions... and then we'll be able to take a sneak peek at whatever it is that Rerir has really been hiding.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (...Whew.)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (Could this be his office?)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (Pretty standard setup. Bookshelves, paperwork, files...)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (According to Dainsleif, Rerir used to be an intelligence operative. Chances are, there's plenty of top-secret intel stashed away in this room.)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (Is this where you keep your secrets, Rerir? Can't say I'm not looking forward to this...)

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Rerir! Are you there?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Hey, Rerir! Come out, it's urgent!

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Dain? What's wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Quick, come with me. I'll explain everything once we've met up with the others.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: I... Okay, I'll come. But Tholindis is still over at the Universitas. I'll need to leave her a note.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Alright then, but make it quick.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: (I've never seen Dain so worked up before. Whatever this is, it must be big trouble.)

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Today's files are in. Time to wade through them, just like usual...

dialogues.speaker: File Content
dialogues.text: ■■■. Male, 51. Occupation: cook. Confirmed Crimson Moon descendant. Has maintained frequent contact with other descendants over the past year. Poses a threat to the dynasty.

dialogues.speaker: File Content
dialogues.text: Neutralized on ■/■.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: This one should be archived under "Purged Targets."

dialogues.speaker: File Content
dialogues.text: ■■. Female, 23. Occupation: office clerk. Confirmed Crimson Moon descendant. Has maintained frequent contact with other descendants over the past year. Poses a threat to the dynasty.

dialogues.speaker: File Content
dialogues.text: Neutralized on ■/■.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Another one for "Purged Targets."

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: (...Sounds like she was that other man's daughter.)

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: (Never mind. What's it got to do with me?)

dialogues.speaker: File Content
dialogues.text: ■■■■■. Male, 40. Occupation: teacher. Confirmed Crimson Moon descendant. Has been observed making contact with other descendants during the past year. Poses a threat to the dynasty.

dialogues.speaker: File Content
dialogues.text: Neutralized on ■/■.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Just another nobody for the archive.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: (Come to think of it, I remember surveilling this man... A case like his would never have been considered a priority in the past. He barely even interacted with other Crimson Moon descendants.)

dialogues.speaker: File Content
dialogues.text: ■■■. Female, 16. Occupation: none. Orphan, and confirmed Crimson Moon descendant. Has been observed making contact with other descendants during the past year. Poses a threat to the dynasty.

dialogues.speaker: File Content
dialogues.text: Neutralized on ■/■.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Filed.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: (I have no recollection of this girl... None, whatsoever. She doesn't seem to be anyone important... but then again, how many of them really are?)

dialogues.speaker: File Content
dialogues.text: ■■■. Female, 13. Occupation: none. Orphan, and confirmed Crimson Moon descendant. Has been observed making contact with other descendants during the past year. Poses a threat to the dynasty.

dialogues.speaker: File Content
dialogues.text: Neutralized on ■/■.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Filed.

dialogues.speaker: File Content
dialogues.text: ■■. Male, 11. Occupation: none. Orphan, and confirmed Crimson Moon descendant. Has not been observed making any contact with other descendants during the past year. Poses a threat to the dynasty.

dialogues.speaker: File Content
dialogues.text: Neutralized on ■/■.

dialogues.speaker: File Content
dialogues.text: ■■. Male, 6. Occupation: none. Orphan, and confirmed Crimson Moon descendant. Poses a threat to the dynasty.

dialogues.speaker: Abyssal Whisper
dialogues.text: It's funny, isn't it? Your job is becoming both harder and easier at the same time, depending on how you look at it.

dialogues.speaker: Abyssal Whisper
dialogues.text: Sooner or later, the Crimson Moon descendants will be completely wiped out. But as their numbers dwindle, they become harder and harder to track down.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: ...That's not how it is.

dialogues.speaker: Abyssal Whisper
dialogues.text: Fortunately, however, most of the able-bodied adults have already been taken care of. The remaining weaklings will be increasingly easy to deal with...

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: No!

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: No.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: My job is to ensure the survival of the Eclipse Dynasty — and the only way to do that is by eliminating any and all potential threats. It's a perfectly legitimate line of work.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Every single one of my colleagues can attest to my fairness, and if my friends were aware of the facts, I know they'd back me up too.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Assuming, of course, that they were aware of all of the facts...

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Mr. Vedrfolnir... It's been quite some time since we last met.

dialogues.speaker: Vedrfolnir
dialogues.text: Rerir. I trust you're here because you have something important to discuss.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Ah, forgive me. I wasn't tuning out, it's just... I notice you didn't even phrase that as a question. As if you knew I was coming.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Tell me — does someone in your position ever feel the need to ask questions at all?

dialogues.speaker: Vedrfolnir
dialogues.text: It is indeed within my power to foresee certain things. Things like your arrival.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: I was just thinking, it won't be long before I'll be inviting both you and Dain to my wedding.

dialogues.speaker: Vedrfolnir
dialogues.text: That isn't a lie... But nor is it a fact, as such. It's a wish, isn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: No fooling a prophet, is there?

dialogues.speaker: Vedrfolnir
dialogues.text: Ever since that day we met for drinks, I knew it was only a matter of time before you came looking for me.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Does it feel good, knowing how the future will unfold?

dialogues.speaker: Vedrfolnir
dialogues.text: I'm afraid the notions of "good" and "bad" fail to capture the complexity of what such a power entails. Once you've seen what will come to pass, it can be all too easy to succumb to fear and melancholy — unless, of course, you learn to abandon these feelings.

dialogues.speaker: Vedrfolnir
dialogues.text: You fear my silence, and long to hear the words I left unspoken that day.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: That's right.

dialogues.speaker: Vedrfolnir
dialogues.text: Hehehe... You must have noticed my reluctance to broach the subject, and the reason is simple — because the truth could never have lived up to your hopes. For both our sakes, such words are better left unsaid.

dialogues.speaker: Vedrfolnir
dialogues.text: The burden of prophecy was never meant for your shoulders.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: So, who exactly do you deem worthy to hear your prophecies? None but our exalted king?

dialogues.speaker: Vedrfolnir
dialogues.text: ...Or rather, our king as he once was.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: You're closer to His Majesty than I am. You must know better than anyone how much he's changed.

dialogues.speaker: Vedrfolnir
dialogues.text: You say that as though it is to my benefit. Yet precisely because of that, I dare not speak rashly. A king can turn out to be the most virtuous of rulers... or a tyrant more terrible than the most vicious of dragons.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: You are so wise and far-sighted, yet still, you would have me live in fear of the unknown.

dialogues.speaker: Vedrfolnir
dialogues.text: Hmm... You make a fair point. Especially given my silence alone was all it took to send you spiraling downwards.

dialogues.speaker: Vedrfolnir
dialogues.text: Very well, then.

dialogues.speaker: Vedrfolnir
dialogues.text: Let me offer you some advice — and I say this not as a "prophet" or a "visionary," but simply as the brother of your friend.

dialogues.speaker: Vedrfolnir
dialogues.text: For many reasons, there is very little chance of your marriage ending in happiness. If happiness is what you seek, you should find another fiancee.

talks.objective: Investigate the black mist in the space

dialogues.speaker: Orlog
dialogues.text: Wait... Hear me out. This time, we finally got a clear look at his face and learned his true identity.

dialogues.speaker: Orlog
dialogues.text: His name is Rerir, and he claims to be one of the king's guards.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: ...What did you say!?

dialogues.speaker: Orlog
dialogues.text: A cruel irony, isn't it... the man you're set to marry leads a double life as a brutal executioner.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: Why are you telling me all of this now?

dialogues.speaker: Orlog
dialogues.text: Simple. It's because...

dialogues.speaker: Orlog
dialogues.text: ...I want you to kill him. You are the only person he would never suspect.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: No... Absolutely not! I would never dream of doing such a despicable thing!

dialogues.speaker: Orlog
dialogues.text: So you'll just stand by and watch him slaughter us to the last? Do not forget that the blood of the Crimson Moon flows in your veins too!

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: The blood of the Crimson Moon... What does that matter now? The dynasty has long been dead and gone.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: You think that alone is reason enough for me to throw away everything I have?

dialogues.speaker: Orlog
dialogues.text: ...Why wouldn't it be?

dialogues.speaker: Orlog
dialogues.text: You too were once a child of the Crimson Moon, just like me. Don't tell me you've never felt so much as a flicker of fury for the way we were trampled into the dust.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: As long as you promise to abandon this pipe dream of restoring your dynasty... I can try to persuade him, or have him persuade the Vinster King.

dialogues.speaker: Orlog
dialogues.text: Persuade, the Vinster King? Haha... Hahahaha...

dialogues.speaker: Orlog
dialogues.text: Do you even know why he's so obsessed with hunting us down? Why he keeps trying to force us to hand over our secrets, over and over again? Or why we refuse to give up on restoring the dynasty?

dialogues.speaker: Orlog
dialogues.text: The Vinster King... a blind fool, his eyes clouded by powers from beyond this world... a petty little man with a miser's heart! And he dares to sit upon the throne? Mark my words — sooner or later Khaenri'ah will fall, and it will be his doing!

dialogues.speaker: Orlog
dialogues.text: If you can't bring yourself to do it, so be it. Just you watch... It won't be long before calamity descends upon us all.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: The "Rächer of Solnari"...

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: That really is quite a secret you've been keeping from me, Rerir.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: But... who am I to talk? Am I really any better? I've kept my own past a secret this whole time too.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: Love should be built on honesty, but ours was born from lies. And yet...

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: Is it really so wrong to hide things that would only make life harder? If we don't cover up the parts that no one else should see, how can we go on pretending to be normal?

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: Vedrfolnir must have known all this, and that's why he made his prophecy. Hah... In the end, nothing stays hidden forever.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: But I won't just sit by and watch this disaster unfold. I'll do everything in my power to protect what I cannot afford to lose...

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: No matter who I have to face.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Monsters!? Is this Rhinedottir's doing? Or the Universitas Magistrorum?

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Out of my way!

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: (The Universitas... That reminds me of a rumor I once heard.)

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: (Allegedly, the king installed secret mechanisms in the palace and around the city. No one knows where they are or what kind of power they hold...)

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: (But if they were ever gonna activate, it would probably be on a night like tonight...)

dialogues.speaker: Person Crying for Help
dialogues.text: Help, heeelp!!!

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Hold on! Don't let them anywhere near you!

dialogues.speaker: Person Crying for Help
dialogues.text: Save me, I can't... Aaah!

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: (That sounded like an explosion... So, the rumor is true? The king really went through with it?)

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: (What other means does the king have at his disposal? They must run on power from the Abyss...)

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: (And given it's a major center of Abyss research, anyone over at the Universitas will be in grave danger. I have to hurry!)

talks.objective: Investigate the black mist in the space

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (He looks even gloomier than last time. I wonder what's changed?)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (Bookshelves full of documents.)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (Looks like these are all files... packed with the personal details of individual Khaenri'ahns...)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (The Crimson Moon Dynasty preceded the Eclipse. Since Rerir worked as a secret agent during the latter, it stands to reason that he was tasked with purging remnants of the old dynasty.)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (Yep. Lines up exactly with what Dainsleif told me.)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (A file tucked inside a folder. The title reads: "Dear Breakfast Shop Owner.")

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (It's... a list of names.)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (But at this stage, I have no idea who any of them even are.)

talks.objective: Investigate the black mist in the space

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: Author: Tholindis

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: Over the course of this week, the research object was subjected to interference for a total of 47 hours for experimental purposes. The results are as follows:

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: ...All subjects of observation that were sent inside have now ■■■■■. The situation within is proving more problematic than anticipated.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: No progress whatsoever... *sigh* What now? Won't you give me even a glimmer of hope?

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: Things are getting worse by the day. I have to find a way, or we'll all be in danger.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: But... But I...

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: *sigh*...

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: If all this research comes to nothing, what then? Sooner or later, it'll be my neck on the line...

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: But... Could he really bring himself to kill me?

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: No... Surely he wouldn't have the heart...

talks.objective: Investigate the black mist in the space

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Today's files are in. Time to wade through them, just like usual...

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: No, I don't get tired of it. It's my job — and not only am I lucky to have it, I'm good at it too.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: ...Wait, that's...!?

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Tholindis?

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: No, no... No!

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Why, why, why!? But you bear no mark of the Crimson Moon!

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: How could you possibly have anything to do with them? It cannot be...

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: *sigh* A diluted bloodline, carefully concealed... I see it now. You've been living in the shadows, just like me.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: What a fool I've been... Numbing myself with talk of justice, even imagining my friends would back me up. But in the end, I...

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Irminsul... Vinster King! How far are you going to take this!? From the direct bloodline, to secondary offshoots... and then what?

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Today, it's the descendants of the Crimson Moon. Who will it be tomorrow? Will you not rest until everyone down here is dead!?

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: No... This cannot go on! This is where it ends!

dialogues.speaker: Frithr
dialogues.text: Tholindis... Do you still remember Orlog?

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: Orlog...

dialogues.speaker: Frithr
dialogues.text: The boy who was pretending to sell flowers. You spoke for quite a while, didn't you?

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: ...Yes, we did.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: What about him?

dialogues.speaker: Frithr
dialogues.text: He... was arrested two days ago. Chances are he's already dead.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: H—He...

dialogues.speaker: Frithr
dialogues.text: I just don't get it... After everything he's done, why do you still stand by him?

dialogues.speaker: Frithr
dialogues.text: Or does it mean nothing to you that people keep dying?

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: No! That's not... Just hear me out!

dialogues.speaker: Frithr
dialogues.text: I need to go now, Tholindis... They're looking for us. You take care too.

dialogues.speaker: Frithr
dialogues.text: If... If you ever need a place to hide, come find us.

dialogues.speaker: Rhinedottir
dialogues.text: Well, this is a nice change, meeting you all at this hour. When men and woman of ambition can speak face to face in broad daylight, I say that's a big step forward for our dear Khaenri'ah.

dialogues.speaker: Surtalogi
dialogues.text: Don't be ridiculous. We do not fear the day. Why would we seek refuge in the night?

dialogues.speaker: Rhinedottir
dialogues.text: You might ask your blade that same question. I'm told it prefers the cover of darkness.

dialogues.speaker: Rhinedottir
dialogues.text: The word on the street is that Surtalogi only strikes when he has an unfair advantage... But that is patently false. I see you're missing an arm and a leg — surely only a fair fight could explain that?

dialogues.speaker: Surtalogi
dialogues.text: If this is your way of offering me replacement limbs, believe me, I'll take them...

dialogues.speaker: Rhinedottir
dialogues.text: Oh, we can certainly discuss that. With Bio-Alchemy, anything is possible — assuming I have your full support in my research.

dialogues.speaker: Surtalogi
dialogues.text: Hmph. Lunatic.

dialogues.speaker: Surtalogi
dialogues.text: Hroptatyr, what brings you here?

dialogues.speaker: Hroptatyr
dialogues.text: Why, Dainsleif, of course. He invited me.

dialogues.speaker: Hroptatyr
dialogues.text: Please, cast aside your apprehensions, Ms Rhinedottir. Whatever the rumors may say, I am but a humble servant of the king, and I can assure you he affords me no greater convenience than he does you.

dialogues.speaker: Rhinedottir
dialogues.text: Well, the Universitas Magistrorum won't stop fawning over you, so at least some of the rumors must be true. You're clearly doing well for yourself — so drop the "humble servant" act. It endears you to no one.

dialogues.speaker: Rhinedottir
dialogues.text: You're president of the Universitas Magistrorum, the Chief Royal Mage known as "The Wise" by royal appointment, and by far the most favored among the Four Pillars of Khaenri'ah.

dialogues.speaker: Rhinedottir
dialogues.text: Vice-President Vit doesn't even try to hide his envy when he sees you.

dialogues.speaker: Hroptatyr
dialogues.text: My success is a product of hard work and good luck, it's as simple as that. Were the king not such an extremist, I hardly think I would've received a senior post at my age.

dialogues.speaker: Hroptatyr
dialogues.text: Of course, no job is without its gripes. Serving a king like ours can be a challenging task, as I'm sure you can imagine.

dialogues.speaker: Hroptatyr
dialogues.text: And as for Eftirvit, in missing out on the presidency, he's dodged a mountain of stress. Like everything else in life, it comes with pros and cons.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Hah... You're all here. I apologize for the short notice, but it was an emergency.

dialogues.speaker: Surtalogi
dialogues.text: You must be Rerir.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Mr. Surtalogi. Yes, I handled your case file during your sentencing — nothing personal, of course. I'm pleasantly surprised that you remember me.

dialogues.speaker: Surtalogi
dialogues.text: You're clearly a person of substance if you've been invited here. But Dainsleif, you'd better have a very good reason for convening this little gathering.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: It's my brother, Vedrfolnir... After he spoke at the court this morning, the king was so infuriated by his words that he had him blinded in both eyes and thrown in prison.

dialogues.speaker: Rhinedottir
dialogues.text: Vedrfolnir, in prison? Strange... I thought the king trusted him and Hroptatyr more than anyone else in the world.

dialogues.speaker: Rhinedottir
dialogues.text: Does this mean the king's circle of trust just got even smaller?

dialogues.speaker: Hroptatyr
dialogues.text: It has nothing to do with trust. It's about what the king wants, which is as clear as day to anyone paying attention.

dialogues.speaker: Hroptatyr
dialogues.text: I simply appease him, because it's in the best interests of the Universitas Magistrorum.

dialogues.speaker: Rhinedottir
dialogues.text: And also because you're slimy. Vedrfolnir, perhaps less so... But still, a visionless visionary? Heh, it rather inclines me to think that qualifications are not what get you ahead in Khaenri'ah.

dialogues.speaker: Surtalogi
dialogues.text: Do you honestly think this is an important discussion to be having right now?

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Dain, what are you planning to do?

dialogues.speaker: Surtalogi
dialogues.text: Rescue Vedrfolnir, I assume?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Correct. It will mean storming the palace by force, tonight. I need all of you on my side.

dialogues.speaker: Hroptatyr
dialogues.text: That's far too dangerous! And don't forget, Dainsleif, you're captain of the royal guard... You swore an oath to the throne.

dialogues.speaker: Rhinedottir
dialogues.text: Hmm? You've... been planning this for a while, haven't you?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: I have no desire to commit treason. But whatever critique the king may have of Vedrfolnir, disfiguring your most loyal subject for putting the best interests of his court and nation first... This is not the conduct of a wise ruler.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: My blade will force the king to see the error of his ways.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: (So, Vedrfolnir's prophecy enraged the king... I'm sure it wasn't what he wanted to hear, but if he won't take counsel even from The Visionary, that is deeply troubling news.)

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: (The extent of His Majesty's madness is now all too clear... The question is, how does a man like me get out of this situation unscathed?)

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: (You have noble ambitions, Dain, but I'm afraid they don't do much for a guy like me. I'm not interested in saving the world — all I want is a letter of pardon.)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: A letter of pardon? For whom? ...Tholindis?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: The chances of the Vinster King issuing a pardon for anyone connected to the Crimson Moon seem vanishingly slim.

talks.objective: Investigate the black mist on the board
Investigate the black mist on the board

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: Author: Tholindis

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: Over the course of this week, the research object was subjected to interference for a total of 60 hours for experimental purposes. The results are as follows:

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: Research dating back to the Crimson Moon dynasty has established two points regarding Moon Marrow. Firstly, its origins have something to do with a god's power. Secondly, it serves as a portal to an as-yet indeterminate location. Moon Marrow can thus be defined as a spatial gateway.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: However, there are a number of hurdles to overcome before we can answer the question of where it leads to. To start with, opening the gateway requires a specific power source, which the relevant literature indicates ■■■■...

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: An enormous amount of power is then required to keep the gate open. Currently, the total power output of our instruments remains in the single digits...

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: To make matters worse, I am now the only staff member remaining in the Moon Marrow lab. The Universitas Magistrorum recently decided to move most of its personnel into Abyssal Energy research, which has stymied all Crimson Moon-related projects.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: This is not a wise move. I have always maintained that placing all our hopes in a single source of power is risky, especially one as poorly understood as this. As well as making ourselves overly reliant on a single resource, we are neglecting other promising technologies.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: I apologize if this comes across as disrespectful. But as a Moon Marrow researcher, I desperately want to see the world beyond the gateway.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: If we really made it there one day, what would we find? And how would we go about taming the unknown? My imagination is endlessly fueled by questions such as these.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: This is for you. I heard you're gonna leave the city with your parents.

dialogues.speaker: Frithr
dialogues.text: Tholindis... Did you hear about... what happened?

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: I've heard nothing. Rerir got back very late last Friday, and he was acting a little unusual. But he slept pretty well, so I'm guessing whatever he did was a good deed.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: You never saw him, and I don't know what he did. And this conversation never happened. You understand?

dialogues.speaker: Frithr
dialogues.text: What if he finds out that you pried into his secrets?

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: Don't be silly. I don't know what secrets he does or doesn't have. All I know is, he's just a normal guy who happens to run some errands for the king.

dialogues.speaker: Frithr
dialogues.text: ...Are you scared of him?

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: I don't know.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: The Rerir I know doesn't match the person you all describe.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: Logically, I should be scared of him. And yet, I don't want to lose him...

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: ...But enough about that. You should get going — and be careful with the package I gave you. Keep it secret... Keep it safe.

dialogues.speaker: Frithr
dialogues.text: What's in it?

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: A piece of the moon. All you need to know is that as long as you keep it safe, then in the future, everyone will be able to see a red moon.

dialogues.speaker: Frithr
dialogues.text: A Red moon? You mean... our moon?

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: That's right. Our moon. Promise me you'll look after it?

dialogues.speaker: Frithr
dialogues.text: I promise, Tholindis!

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: The Crimson Moon bloodline will never die out. Its light, the color of blood, will become like a fire that flows in our veins.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: No matter how long it takes...

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Hurry, everyone, and stick to the plan!

dialogues.speaker: Royal Guard
dialogues.text: Sir Dainsleif!? What are you... Is this treason?

dialogues.speaker: Royal Guard
dialogues.text: You know what happens to those who betray the throne! Please, don't do this!

dialogues.speaker: Surtalogi
dialogues.text: It is the king himself who has betrayed the throne. He has betrayed all of Khaenri'ah.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: If you have any love left for justice in your heart, you should join me.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: (It's showtime. Dain and his group will handle the troops in the palace, then Hroptatyr and Rhinedottir will disarm the security measures.)

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: (My job is to enter the prison and rescue Vedrfolnir.)

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Stay safe! Wish me luck!

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Look after my brother!

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Draw your blade. It is time for justice to prevail!

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: This place is filthy... and the smell is abominable. Clearly, the king doesn't allow his prisoners a single shred of dignity. This is dire.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Found you. Hello, Mr. Vedrfolnir.

dialogues.speaker: Vedrfolnir
dialogues.text: Ah. It's you.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Surprised? No, wait... I guess surprise isn't an emotion that prophets feel very often.

dialogues.speaker: Vedrfolnir
dialogues.text: I certainly felt some surprise in the moment when I was blinded. Surprise at the king's sheer ignorance. Surprise at just how unfairly this world responds to words of earnest remonstration.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: I'm curious, what did you prophesize this time?

dialogues.speaker: Vedrfolnir
dialogues.text: It wasn't a prophecy, it was a word of warning. Someone had to say it.

dialogues.speaker: Vedrfolnir
dialogues.text: The king has forsaken all reason in pursuit of his obsessions. I simply told him that if he continues on this path, Khaenri'ah will surely fall.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: But he didn't listen. Worse still, he stabbed you in both eyes and locked you away.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Dain asked for my help. The court is in complete chaos now, but I'm sure you predicted that.

dialogues.speaker: Vedrfolnir
dialogues.text: Everything is transpiring as I foresaw, yet I am powerless to change it... Fate is an immutable force. I can but lament as the inevitable unfolds.

dialogues.speaker: Vedrfolnir
dialogues.text: I do wonder whether giving a man the power to see the future does nothing more for him than slowly crush his spirits...

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Forgive my curtness, Vedrfolnir, but the king did not suddenly turn on you today. His suspicions have been brewing for a long time.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: You can't have wisdom beyond the reach of your fellow man without attracting his fear and suspicion.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: There are things the king does not want to see, so he doesn't want you having visions of them either. He blinded you because he thought this would make the visions stop.

dialogues.speaker: Vedrfolnir
dialogues.text: He wasn't entirely wrong. I did indeed lose my power to see the future... right up until...

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Until what?

dialogues.speaker: Vedrfolnir
dialogues.text: Just now... I believe I saw something new.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Well, tonight could go a lot of different ways. Five of us banded together to storm the palace — all so we could rescue you. This will go down as the most tumultuous day in Khaenri'ahn history.

dialogues.speaker: Vedrfolnir
dialogues.text: I sense hatred in you... but also hope. A desperate hope that with the tyrant deposed, that will be the end of the story.

dialogues.speaker: Vedrfolnir
dialogues.text: But this is not the end. It is the beginning of a new chapter in a whole new story.

dialogues.speaker: Vedrfolnir
dialogues.text: There are many men of honor and courage in this world, Rerir, but you are not one of them. You're not here for justice, are you? You're here for yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Vedrfolnir
dialogues.text: Is that a dagger? Interesting. Why not the polearm? It was always your weapon of choice.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: With your abilities, I don't doubt that you were able to recover some of your sight. But I also doubt that you want to make an enemy of me right now.

dialogues.speaker: Vedrfolnir
dialogues.text: Of course not. We're on the same side, aren't we?

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: We could be. But I need you to be honest with me, Vedrfolnir. At this point, you're my only hope for the future.

dialogues.speaker: Vedrfolnir
dialogues.text: You mean, your future? With your beloved, Tholindis?

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Yes. And I know there are bigger things at stake here — a dynasty, a nation, maybe the entire world... But forgive me, I care first and foremost about myself.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: I can't abandon the one I love to save myself. I just can't do it. But you see a broader picture of the future than I. You see the solutions to the biggest problems of our age... So tell me, what is my solution? What's the answer?

dialogues.speaker: Vedrfolnir
dialogues.text: In matters of fate, answers are either right or wrong: what will be, and what will not. Maybe you are willing to pay a certain price in the pursuit of happiness, but unfortunately, fate does not negotiate.

dialogues.speaker: Vedrfolnir
dialogues.text: That is the cruelest thing about fate. It is unmoved by your sacrifices.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: That can't be true!

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: I know it's your voice that I keep hearing in my head... urging me to see how the world is changing, to seek more power so I can protect the things I love...

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: You show me disaster, but you won't show me how to avoid it... Why? Why are you doing all this?

dialogues.speaker: Vedrfolnir
dialogues.text: My voice? In your head?

dialogues.speaker: Vedrfolnir
dialogues.text: Haha... Hahahaha... So, you hear it too. The voice that steals your mind, gains your trust, and drives you crazy...

dialogues.speaker: Vedrfolnir
dialogues.text: It turns out that we are not so different, you and I.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: (Vedrfolnir just broke into the strangest smile I've ever seen in my life, as if he'd discovered some monumental secret. But then he suddenly switched to looking extremely weary.)

dialogues.speaker: Vedrfolnir
dialogues.text: Very well then. My advice to you is as follows: You must persevere. Whatever trials and tribulations you may face, be steadfast in the belief that they are your path to the future.

dialogues.speaker: Vedrfolnir
dialogues.text: For as long as you live, your story with Tholindis shall not come to an end. That is the only chance you have of fighting back against fate.

dialogues.speaker: Vedrfolnir
dialogues.text: It is up to you whether you believe my words. Regardless, that is all I will say on the matter. I have no right to intervene any further.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: I will hold you to your word.

dialogues.speaker: Vedrfolnir
dialogues.text: Thank you for setting me free. In return, I will tell you one more thing that you cannot afford to ignore...

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: (Just then, a strange wave of energy rippled through the city. We had no idea what it could mean.)

dialogues.speaker: Vedrfolnir
dialogues.text: If I were you, I would head to the Universitas Magistrorum.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: The Universitas... Oh no!

dialogues.speaker: Vedrfolnir
dialogues.text: I'm sure we'll be seeing each other again very soon, Rerir.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: (Whatever Vedrfolnir said, I didn't catch it. I didn't even help him out of the prison. There was no time to lose.)

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: Monsters, at the Universitas Magistrorum? Why now!?

dialogues.speaker: Monsters
dialogues.text: Grrr...

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: Oh no, they're coming...

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: It's no use, the table won't hold out much longer... The weapons... Where are the weapons?

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: ...Of course. All the lab equipment was upgraded after the inspection last week, but the new weapons haven't been allocated yet...

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: I'm done for... Is anyone there!? I need help!!!

dialogues.speaker: Monsters
dialogues.text: Roar!

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: Stay back... please stay back, please...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (Wonder what kind of encryption technique this is... Hmm, seems like it has to be inserted into that camouflaged device nearby.)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (Aha... It's an audio recording.)

dialogues.speaker: Audio Recording
dialogues.text: Please, hear me out... I can't shake this feeling that someone's been spying on our house... No, I'm not being paranoid, it's true!

dialogues.speaker: Audio Recording
dialogues.text: I saw someone dressed in all black... It was a couple of days back, but that was on another street, not near my house... I swear, I know what I saw!

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (There's a note in the margin: Surveillance of the Runvorthr residence has concluded. We apprehended the target and filed the mission report last night.)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (Could the voice in the recording belong to one of Rerir's targets?)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (A box containing a ring inlaid with a precious gem...)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (Must be for his girlfriend...)

dialogues.speaker: Examine the Board
dialogues.text: (There are some handwritten messages on the whiteboard...)

dialogues.speaker: Notes on the Board
dialogues.text: "I took the time to do a few sketches that represent the staffing for different units."

dialogues.speaker: Notes on the Board
dialogues.text: "The art's pretty good, huh? Bet you'll all like it. Mika always used to say I had the talent to make it big."

dialogues.speaker: Examine the Board
dialogues.text: (These seem to have been written by Varka...?)

dialogues.speaker: Examine the Board
dialogues.text: (Another message appears after these lines, written in a different hand:)

dialogues.speaker: Words Written in a Different Hand
dialogues.text: "Your creative work has, by the testimony of our fellow knights, proved excellent food for thought, Grand Master Varka."

dialogues.speaker: Words Written in a Different Hand
dialogues.text: "I have looked through it carefully, and I suspect this is because your work is novel, yet your technique remains slightly unpolished."

dialogues.speaker: Words Written in a Different Hand
dialogues.text: "This is only natural, of course. After all, you have never received any formal education in art."

dialogues.speaker: Words Written in a Different Hand
dialogues.text: "In accordance with requests I have received, I shall complete a few new paintings to serve as mementos for everyone."

dialogues.speaker: Words Written in a Different Hand
dialogues.text: "P.S.: Please understand that the Grand Master almost always has his hands full defending others — that his artistic capabilities are developed as this is a testament to the time he has spent alongside Spark Knight Klee."

dialogues.speaker: Words Written in a Different Hand
dialogues.text: (The writer has signed off in the corner as "Albedo.")

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Hold on, there's that same black fog again. Could this memory belong to Tholindis?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: ...Guess I'd better tread carefully.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: This black fog over the board must have some connection to Tholindis. But why is it taking this form? Does it have something to do with Rerir's past?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Another mystery I'll need to unravel...

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: *panting*...

dialogues.speaker: Orlog
dialogues.text: Why won't you just let us go? We don't even know each other... All we want is to live ordinary, peaceful lives!

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: You want... to live?

dialogues.speaker: Orlog
dialogues.text: Yes... I just want to go on living.

dialogues.speaker: Orlog
dialogues.text: Is that really such an unforgivable crime?

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Hah... You want to "go on living."

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: I want to keep living, too... to keep living forever. That's why I have no choice but to continue on the path I'm on.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: If only some savior would suddenly swoop down and change the way the world is... Too bad that's not going to happen.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Let the simulation begin.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Imagine that. If there really were such a person, you and I wouldn't be standing here like this, would we?

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Monsters!? Is this Rhinedottir's doing? Or the Universitas Magistrorum?

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Out of my way!
